chapter.title: Chapter {count}
chapter.resumed: Chapter {count} · {name} reread its memory and picked up where it left off
chapter.explainer: When a chapter fills up, {name} saves what matters to memory and starts with a clean page. The conversation stays whole in the window, and each new message doesn't cost more.
chapter.usageHint: How much of the current chapter is used
memory.title: Memory
memory.smartDesc: New chapter when the conversation grows, and a fresh start each morning. Fits almost everyone.
memory.dailyDesc: A clean page every morning. Good for assistants with daily tasks.
memory.fullDesc: The agent compresses old messages itself. Handy for one big task, but costs more.
memory.memoryFile: Main points: projects, decisions, open tasks · updated at {time}
memory.footer: Plain Markdown files on your server. You can open, edit or delete them. The agent reads the new version in the next chapter.

settings.title: Settings
settings.approvalsIntro: Bandito checks every action an agent takes. Routine work runs on its own, while anything that matches a rule below or a built-in check waits for your decision.
rules.when: When the agent wants to run
rules.wildcardNote: * matches anything. If two rules match, a rule for a specific agent wins, then the newer one.
rules.builtinHint: always apply unless a rule above says otherwise
server.add.title: Add server
server.add.heading: Connect a server
server.add.intro: The code stays on your server. Choose how this Mac reaches it. Every option gives the same encrypted connection.
server.add.thisMacDesc: Runs right here. Nothing to set up.
server.add.sshDesc: Uses your ~/.ssh/config. Bandito installs itself and connects over the same link.
server.add.tailscaleDesc: Any computer on your Tailscale network. No SSH and no open ports.
server.add.directDesc: Address and port, a pinned certificate, and a code of six words.
server.add.urlDesc: Cloudflare Tunnel, WireGuard, a reverse proxy — any URL that reaches the daemon.
server.add.relayDesc: Outbound only, end-to-end encrypted. Works behind any NAT.
server.add.keysHint: keys and jump hosts are used as they are
server.add.codeHint: Run `bandito pair` on the server and type the six words.
server.add.install: Bandito isn't installed there yet. Install it now?
server.add.privacy: We open no ports. The daemon listens only on the server itself, and the app connects through an SSH tunnel.
onboarding.welcome.headline: Your AI team.
onboarding.welcome.subtitle: Agents on Claude Code, Codex and Grok, with roles and schedules. They keep working when you close your laptop, and ask before anything risky.
onboarding.welcome.sleepText: Agents live on your server. Close your Mac and they keep going, then send you the result in the morning.
onboarding.welcome.askText: Pushes, deploys, deletes — only with your yes. Answer from the Mac, from a notification, or from an iPhone.
onboarding.welcome.subsText: Claude, ChatGPT (Codex) or Grok — Bandito runs their official programs. No new accounts.
onboarding.welcome.footer: Open source · your code and keys never leave your servers
onboarding.welcome.serverText: Files, terminals, browser and the server screen in one window. Easier than SSH, and agents see what you see.
onboarding.demo.user: Update the dependencies, run the tests and open a PR.
onboarding.demo.askPush: Forge wants to push a branch
onboarding.demo.done: Done: opened PR #44, tests are green. Scout is already looking.
onboarding.account.heroTitle: One team — on Mac and iPhone
onboarding.account.heroText: Sign in once and all your servers and agents show up on every device. Approve tasks from your phone, even when the Mac is closed.
onboarding.account.title: Create your Bandito account
onboarding.account.subtitle: It's free, and it lets your devices find each other. You won't need to make up a password.
onboarding.account.privacy: We only store your list of servers — encrypted, and only your devices hold the key. Code, API keys and conversations stay on your servers.
onboarding.account.skipHint: everything stays on this Mac only
tour.agents.title: Your agents
tour.agents.text: Each agent is its own chat. The orange dot means someone is waiting for your decision.
tour.composer.title: Write like to a colleague
tour.composer.text: Plain words work: “add tests and open a PR”. Type / for the commands.
tour.approvals.title: Risky steps wait for you
tour.approvals.text: Pushes, deploys and deletes come to you. Allow or deny here, or on your phone.
tour.quickOpen.title: Find anything with ⌘K
tour.quickOpen.text: Agents, folders, terminals and settings: start typing.
tour.modes.title: Files and terminals
tour.modes.text: Switch modes with ⌘1…⌘6: the server's files, terminals, the browser and the screen.
onboarding.subs.title: Connect your subscriptions
onboarding.subs.subtitle: Agents run on the official programs of your subscriptions. Sign in to at least one; the others can wait.
onboarding.subs.needOne: You need at least one signed-in agent to create an agent.
onboarding.subs.hintClaude: Type /login and choose sign-in with your subscription. A link appears: open it on this Mac, then paste the code here.
onboarding.subs.hintCodex: Follow the prompts. If a link appears, open it on this Mac and paste the code back here.
onboarding.subs.hintGrok: Grok shows a device code and a link. Open the link on this Mac, enter the code, then press Done.
onboarding.subs.stateUnverified: installed; the server cannot check the sign-in
onboarding.agent.needSubscription: No agent is signed in yet. Sign in to a subscription first.
onboarding.agent.composerText: Hi! Introduce yourself and ask what to start with.
onboarding.agent.err.badCharacters: Use letters, digits, spaces, dashes and underscores.
onboarding.agent.err.duplicate: An agent with this name already exists.
onboarding.server.invalidAddress: Enter the address as user@host or user@host:port.
onboarding.server.hostKeyScanFailed: Could not read the server's host key. Check the address and try again.
onboarding.server.viaProxy: This server is reached through a jump host. Connect once in Terminal with the command below, and confirm its key there.
onboarding.server.hostKeyChangedWhileRev: The server's key changed while you were checking it. Nothing was trusted. Check the server and start again.
onboarding.server.trustHost: This is my server — trust it
onboarding.server.fingerprintHint: Compare it with the fingerprint your provider or your server shows. If you are not sure, cancel: nothing is trusted until you confirm.
onboarding.server.copyKeyHint: Add this Mac's key to the server once. Run this in Terminal on this Mac, and type the server password when asked:
onboarding.server.passwordHint: Some parts need an administrator password. Bandito never asks for it and never keeps it: run this command in a terminal on the server, then check again.
onboarding.server.err.hostUnknown: This Mac has not seen this server before. Check its fingerprint, then trust it if it is yours.
onboarding.server.err.hostChanged: The server's key is not the one this Mac knows. That can mean someone is in the middle. Nothing is trusted; check the server first.
onboarding.server.err.keyNotAccepted: The server does not accept this Mac's key yet. Add the key once with the command below.
onboarding.server.err.unknownHost: The server name does not resolve. Check the address.
onboarding.server.err.refused: The server refuses the connection. Check that SSH runs on that port.
onboarding.server.err.timedOut: The server does not answer. Check that it is on and reachable.
onboarding.server.err.noRoute: There is no network route to the server from this Mac.
onboarding.server.err.unsupported: This server's system or processor is not supported. Bandito needs Linux or macOS on x86_64 or arm64.
onboarding.server.err.localBinary: The bandito program is missing from this app. Reinstall Bandito.
onboarding.server.err.releaseCheck: Release signature check failed — the download may have been tampered with. Nothing was installed.
onboarding.server.err.generic: The install stopped. Look at the log for the step that failed.
onboarding.account.resetWarning: All other devices will be signed out and the sync settings will be erased. Your servers and the agents on them stay as they are.
onboarding.account.approvalTitle: Confirm this Mac on another device
onboarding.account.approvalSubtitle: Sign-in is done. To use your servers here, another device of yours must approve this Mac.
onboarding.account.approvalHint: Open Bandito on another Mac or iPhone. A request appears there. Compare the code shown on that screen with this one.
onboarding.account.senderTitle: Approved by the device with code {code}. Does it match the code on that screen?
onboarding.account.senderHint: Press “They match” only if the two codes are identical.
onboarding.account.refusedText: The codes differ, so the key was not accepted and nothing was stored. Someone may be trying to get into your account. Don't continue; write to us.
onboarding.account.recoverText: This Mac has no sync key, and no other device can give it one. Restoring resets the account's sync data: other devices are signed out and the sync settings are erased. Your servers and agents stay as they are.
onboarding.account.approveHowTo: The new device shows the same code. Type it here exactly as it appears there.
onboarding.account.approveThisMac: This Mac's code (the new device compares it with its screen):
onboarding.account.bannerText: New device “{name}” ({platform}) wants to sign in
onboarding.account.settingsSignedOut: Sign in to see your devices and to sync your servers.
onboarding.account.codeMismatch: The code does not match this device. Do not approve it.
onboarding.account.noKeyHere: This Mac has no sync key.
onboarding.account.keyUnavailable: Could not read this Mac's device key. Try again.
onboarding.account.setupFailed: Could not start sign-in. Try again.
onboarding.account.codeHint: Enter the 6-digit code we sent to {email}
onboarding.account.resendIn: Send a new code in {seconds} s
onboarding.account.iphoneHint: On iPhone, sign in the same way. Your servers will appear by themselves.
onboarding.account.github.title: Confirm on GitHub
onboarding.account.github.waiting: Waiting for your confirmation on GitHub
onboarding.account.github.expired: The code has expired. Start again.
onboarding.account.github.denied: You declined the sign-in on GitHub.
onboarding.server.title: Where will your team live?
onboarding.server.subtitle: Agents run on a computer that stays on. Use your own server, a home PC, or this Mac just to try things out.
onboarding.server.thisMacDesc: Quick to try. Agents run only while the Mac is awake and open.
onboarding.server.ownServerDesc: Runs around the clock. A VPS, a home PC or a work server — we connect over SSH and install everything ourselves.
onboarding.server.noServerDesc: Any VPS from $5 a month will do. We'll walk you through where to get one and what to click.
onboarding.server.addressHint: This is how you usually sign in over SSH: user@address. We use your keys from {path}, and we won't ask for a password.
onboarding.server.stepInstall: Install Bandito (≈ 20 MB) as a service
onboarding.server.stepLink: Link the server to this Mac
onboarding.server.stepCheck: Check Claude Code, Codex and Grok, and show where to sign in
onboarding.server.noPorts: We open no ports: the server only listens to itself.
onboarding.server.otherWays: Other ways: Tailscale, direct connection, custom address — {link}
onboarding.agent.title: Who do you hire first?
onboarding.agent.subtitle: Pick a ready-made role and we'll set the model, instructions and schedule. You can change everything later, and add new agents any time.
onboarding.agent.firstMessage: The first message takes a few seconds: {name} introduces itself and asks where to start.
template.builder.title: Builder
template.builder.desc: Writes and fixes code, runs tests, opens PRs.
template.builder.instructions: You write and fix code in the project. You make small changes, run the tests before every commit, open a PR, and briefly write what you did.
template.reviewer.title: Reviewer
template.reviewer.desc: Reviews other agents' changes and your PRs, looks for bugs.
template.oncall.title: On-call
template.oncall.desc: Watches production and logs, wakes you only when it matters.
template.oncall.meta: Claude Code · low effort · checks every 15 min
template.assistant.title: Assistant
template.assistant.desc: Mail, calendar, notes, reminders — in plain language.
template.assistant.meta: Claude Code · medium · daily summary at 09:00
template.researcher.title: Researcher
template.researcher.desc: Searches, reads and compares, brings back a digest with links.
template.scratch.title: From scratch
template.scratch.desc: An empty agent: you pick the name, role and instructions.
tour.team.title: This is your team
tour.team.text: Each agent is its own chat. The orange dot means someone is waiting for your decision.
tour.write.title: Write to it like a colleague
tour.write.text: Use plain words: “add tests for payments and open a PR”. The agent works out what to run.
tour.approve.title: Risky things need your yes
tour.approve.text: Pushes, deploys and deletes come to you. Allow with a button, or deny. You can also answer from your phone.
tour.limits.title: See what's left
tour.limits.text: Here you can see how much of your Claude, ChatGPT and Grok limit is left, and when it resets.
team.pickAgent: Pick an agent to see its chat
usage.fallbackNote: If a limit runs out, the agent switches to its backup subscription and returns after the reset. You set this per agent. Updated {time}.
usage.empty: No limits received yet. They appear after the first reply or a refresh.
demo.preview.scout: Approved the changes, left one comment.
demo.preview.watch: All quiet · 5xx 0.02% in the last hour
demo.preview.nightOwl: Next run in 11 h · dependency audit
demo.preview.atlas: Hands tasks out to the team.

gestures.twoFingerSwipe.title: Two-finger swipe — back and forward
gestures.twoFingerSwipe.text: Like Safari and Finder: step back and forward through folders, pages and files.
gestures.agentRow.title: Swipe on an agent — actions
gestures.agentRow.text: Like Mail: left to pin, pause or delete; right to mark as read.
gestures.pinch.title: Pinch — zoom
gestures.pinch.text: Bigger and smaller text in the terminal and files, zoom on the server screen.
gestures.panePinch.title: Pinch out — full screen
gestures.panePinch.text: Spread your fingers over a terminal to expand it; pinch in to go back to the grid.
gestures.forcePress.title: Force click — preview
gestures.forcePress.text: Press harder on an agent, file or link to preview it without opening.
gestures.doubleTap.title: Two-finger double tap
gestures.doubleTap.text: Zoom in on a place on the server screen or on a browser page.

changes.keepHint: Untick a file to put it back as it was before the task. The rest stays.
changes.rollbackConfirmMessage: Files go back to how they were before the task. You can undo this from the notice.

server.processes.stopMessage: Its processes get a stop signal. Those still running after 3 seconds are killed.

server.features.title: Capabilities
server.workspaces.title: Workplaces
server.workspaces.intro: Where agents live: their files, browser, screen and terminals. Keep them together, or seat one apart. Drag an agent to another place and it moves with its next task.
server.workspaces.demoOff: Examples are off, so there is nothing to show. Turn them on in Settings → General.
server.workspaces.compare.sharedText: Quick and simple: agents see the same server you do. Fine when you trust the team.
server.workspaces.compare.userText: Own files, browser and screen. Other things only if you open them. The server itself is shared.
server.workspaces.compare.containerText: Full isolation: own disk, network, and CPU and memory limits. For experiments and code you do not trust.
demo.space.shared.files: the whole server, as the deploy user
secrets.deleteMessage: Agents that had it restart without it.
secrets.empty: No secrets yet. Add a key or password that agents need.
secrets.hint: Agents get secrets as environment variables. Values are never shown in chat.
secrets.nameRule: Capitals, digits and _, up to 64 characters, not starting with a digit. PATH, HOME and similar names are refused.
secrets.valueHint: After saving, only the last four characters are visible. Up to 64 KB.
devices.intro: Phones and Macs that connect to this server. Revoking one cuts off only that device.
devices.revokeMessage: The device loses access to the server at once.
devices.pairIntro: Scan the code with Bandito on the device, or type it in. The code works once.
setup.needsPassword: An administrator password is needed. Run the command in a Bandito terminal and type the password there.
setup.failed: Could not install {component}. See the log above.
settings.account.intro: Sign in to sync servers, shortcuts and prompts between your devices.
settings.account.signedOutHint: Not signed in. Everything works on this Mac without an account.
settings.servers.intro: Servers this app connects to. Each keeps its own agents and settings.
settings.servers.deleteMessage: The app forgets the server and its token. Nothing on the server is deleted.
settings.approvals.intro: Bandito checks each action of an agent. Routine work goes on by itself; everything that matches a rule below or a built-in check waits for you.
settings.approvals.when: When the agent wants to run
settings.approvals.wildcardNote: * means anything. If two rules match, the rule for one agent wins, then the newer one.
settings.approvals.builtinHint: Always checked. A rule for one agent can override them.
settings.approvals.browserChecks: In the browser and on the screen
settings.approvals.touchIDHint: Pushing to main, deploys and deletions wait for a fingerprint on the Mac or Face ID on the iPhone.
settings.approvals.autoDeny: If you do not answer within 30 minutes
settings.approvals.autoDenyHint: Decline and ask the agent to find another way, instead of waiting forever.
settings.usage.intro: Subscriptions and API budgets of your agents. Each bar shows what is left in its window.
settings.workplaces.intro: Where each agent works: its files, browser, screen and terminals.
settings.workplaces.body: Workplaces are set up on the Server screen. Each one is shared with the server, a container, or a separate user.
settings.terminalFiles.intro: How terminals and the file browser look and start.
settings.terminalFiles.fontSizeHint: In new terminals. ⌘+ and ⌘− change it inside a terminal.
settings.terminalFiles.showHiddenHint: When a folder opens. ⌘⇧. toggles it in the file browser.
settings.browserScreen.intro: The server's browser and screen, as you see them on this Mac.
settings.browserScreen.qualityHint: Faster sends less data; sharper uses more bandwidth.
settings.browserScreen.clipboardHint: Copy here, paste there, and the other way round.
settings.notifications.intro: Bandito tells you when an agent needs you. Choose what is worth a notification.
settings.notifications.failedHint: An agent stopped because of a failure.
settings.appearance.intro: How the app looks and moves.
settings.appearance.themeHint: Light and system themes come later.
settings.appearance.motionHint: Off stops all motion in the app, like Reduce Motion in the system.
settings.updates.intro: Versions of this app and of the daemon on your server.
updates.howText: The update runs the same install script as the first setup. It replaces the daemon and keeps your data and settings. Run it in a terminal on the server.
terminals.updateServer: Update the server to use terminals.
terminals.emptyHint: A terminal keeps running on the server, even when this app is closed.
terminals.layouts.mainRight: Main and two on the right
terminals.inputToAllHint: What you type in the focused pane goes to every pane on screen
terminals.noRoom: No room on screen. Collapse or close a pane first.
terminals.confirmClose.title: The process is still running. End it?
terminals.dock.title: Collapsed
terminals.sidebar.noteBody: A collapsed terminal keeps running on the server, even when this Mac is off. Come back and see everything it printed.
browser.title: Browser
browser.hint: The browser lives on the server. Sign-ins are kept, and agents see the same tabs you do. Isolated agents have their own browser.
browser.unsupported: The browser appears after the server is updated
browser.missingChrome: Chrome is needed on the server
screen.title: Server screen
screen.unsupported: The server screen is available on Linux servers
screen.hint: Click the screen or press Take control. The agent waits until you let go.
screen.sleepHint: The screen wakes on demand. After 30 minutes nobody uses it, neither you nor agents, and it sleeps to free the server's memory.
screen.error: Could not connect to the screen
screen.agentBusy: The agent is working on the screen. Take control to type.
agentSheet.apiKeyHint: Any model, pay per token. Coming soon.
agentSheet.modelFreeHint: Any model name the CLI accepts.
agentSheet.effortHintLow: Fast and cheap: for small edits and questions.
agentSheet.effortHintMedium: The higher, the smarter on hard tasks, but slower, and it uses the limit faster. Medium is enough for everyday work.
agentSheet.effortHintHigh: For hard tasks: it thinks longer and uses the limit noticeably faster.
agentSheet.effortHintXhigh: For big rewrites and tangled bugs. The limit runs down fast.
agentSheet.effortHintMax: The deepest thinking. Only when nothing else worked.
agentSheet.fallbackHint: Memory and tasks move with it: it picks up where it left off.
agentSheet.workplaceHint: its files, browser, screen and terminals
agentSheet.workplaceSharedText: Same server as you. Fastest start.
agentSheet.workplaceSoonHint: Separate and container workplaces are coming soon.
agentSheet.statusNotSignedIn: Not signed in on the server
template.reviewer.instructions: You review other agents' changes and the team's PRs. Look for bugs, unsafe changes and missing tests. Leave short, concrete comments and say what must change.
template.oncall.instructions: You watch production and the logs, checking every 15 minutes. Wake the owner only for real problems, and say what you saw and what to do.
template.assistant.instructions: You help with mail, calendar, notes and reminders. Answer in plain language. Every morning at 09:00 send a short summary.
template.researcher.instructions: You search, read and compare sources. Bring back a short digest with links, and say how sure you are of each point.
